commons.title: Christ Pantocrator mosaic from Hagia Sophia 2240 x 3109 pixels 2.5 MB.jpg
commons.description:
Detail of a marvelous mosaic of Christ from the Hagia Sophia in Instanbul. It is the central figure of the so called Deësis mosaic (Δέησις, "Entreaty") which probably dates from a relatively late 1261. It is considered by many to be the finest mosaic in Hagia Sophia. It is also unusually realistic for a byzantine work. Observe for example the depiction of single strands of hair on the beard or of the shadow that falls across Christ's throat.
This is a large and well detailed image, even though I took it with a point and shoot camera. It captures well the physical medium of the mosaic. I believe but only from memory, that the colors are quite realistic too.
commons.editorial_reason: Byzantine Christian mosaic attributed to Antiochian Greek Christian context, not Rum Arabs.

commons.title: Damascus Greek Orthodox Patriarchate 9817.jpg
commons.description: View from the courtyard. One of pictures of (mainly) a specific church, called the Mariamite Cathedral, and also some of the larger complex to which it belongs. A lone minaret nearby is not part of it. The complex houses the seat of the Patriarchate of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch.
commons.editorial_reason: Greek Orthodox Patriarchate architecture is tied to Antiochian Greek Christians, not Rum Arabs.
